mainTopic: Limits on קל וחומר: the פרה אדומה and עגלה ערופה, and what disqualifies כהנים and לוים
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why a פרה אדומה cannot be done with עריפה. At first it says the word 'חוקה' blocks any קל וחומר. It then challenges this from יום הכפורים, which is also called a חוקה, yet still needed a special פסוק to block a קל וחומר. So the גמרא gives a new answer: the word 'הערופה' limits עריפה to the עגלה alone. Another פסוק, 'וערפו', shows the עגלה cannot be done with שחיטה. A new משנה then says some things disqualify כהנים but not לוים, and the reverse. A ברייתא explains that מומין disqualify כהנים, while age disqualifies לוים, and it learns both rules from 'זאת אשר ללוים'. It adds that the age limit applied only while the משכן was carried, and that a לוי trained from 25 and served from 30. From those five years of training it learns a lesson for students, and רבי יוסי says the test period is three years. The amud ends with רבי יוסי asking for the פסוק showing that in שילה and the בית המקדש only a failing voice disqualifies a לוי; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Only slaughter works for the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question: the פסוק says 'ושחט' and calls the פרה אדומה a 'חוקה', so it needs שחיטה and עריפה does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'and he shall slaughter' and uses the word 'statute.' So slaughter, yes. Breaking the neck, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked just before: why not learn from עגלה ערופה that עריפה should also work for a פרה אדומה? The answer is that the פסוק demands שחיטה and adds the word 'חוקה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ושחט' alone tells us how the פרה is normally done. The word 'חוקה' adds that the procedure is fixed and cannot be changed. Together they block any קל וחומר that would allow עריפה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall slaughter' – the פסוק about the פרה אדומה
A 'statute' – a fixed rule that must be done exactly as written
Ritual slaughter by cutting the throat
Breaking the neck, as is done with the עגלה ערופה

phrases.english: The verse says 'and he shall slaughter,' and it says 'statute':
phrases.notes: 'ושחט' is במדבר 19:3; 'זאת חקת התורה' is במדבר 19:2.

phrases.english: with slaughter, yes; with breaking the neck, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about why we do not use a קל וחומר from עגלה ערופה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation: the word 'חוקה' together with 'ושחט' blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קל וחומר from עגלה ערופה would let עריפה work for the פרה אדומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only שחיטה works for the פרה אדומה, because it is a חוקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the principle that the next steps test: does the word 'חוקה' always cancel a קל וחומר?

steps.title: Challenge from the יום הכפורים goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'חוקה' really always blocks a קל וחומר, and begins to quote a ברייתא about יום הכפורים, which is also called a חוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that wherever 'statute' is written, we do not use a קל וחומר? But יום הכפורים is called a 'statute,' and a ברייתא teaches: 'And he shall make it a sin offering' – the lottery makes it a sin offering, but calling it by name does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule from step 1 and brings a ברייתא about the two goats of יום הכפורים. This step only starts the challenge; the punch comes at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים is also called a 'חוקה', so it is a good test case. The ברייתא says that only the lottery (גורל) makes the goat a חטאת; simply naming it does not. The גמרא is about to show that the ברייתא needed a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one: if it is true there, it is surely true here
We expound or derive
The lottery used to choose which goat is for ה׳ on יום הכפורים
Here: a spoken naming of the animal as a חטאת

phrases.english: And anywhere that 'statute' is written about it,
do we not derive a קל וחומר?
But regarding יום הכפורים,
where 'statute' is written about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:34

phrases.english: and it is taught: 'And he shall make it a sin offering' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9

phrases.english: the lottery makes it a sin offering,
and naming it does not make it a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ חוּקָּה, לָא דָּרְשִׁינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle used in step 1, that 'חוקה' blocks a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wherever 'חוקה' is written, a קל וחומר is never used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום הכפורים is called a חוקה, yet a ברייתא treats a קל וחומר there as a real possibility that needed a פסוק to block it.

steps.title: The ברייתא's קל וחומר about naming the goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why the פסוק was needed: without it, we would have used a קל וחומר to say that naming also makes the goat a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought: isn't it logical? If in a case where the lottery does not make something holy, naming does make it holy, then where the lottery does make it holy, surely naming does too! So the verse says: 'And he shall make it a sin offering' – the lottery makes it a sin offering, but naming it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows the קל וחומר it was worried about. Then it shows how the פסוק 'ועשהו חטאת' stops that קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this: in other קרבנות, where there is no lottery at all, naming works. So on יום הכפורים, where even a lottery works, naming should surely work too. The ברייתא answers that the פסוק limits it to the lottery alone, which means that only the פסוק stopped the קל וחומר, not the word 'חוקה'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it logical?' – the standard opening of a קל וחומר
Made the animal holy for a specific קרבן
'The verse teaches' – introduces the פסוק that settles the matter

phrases.english: For one might have thought: is it not logical?
If in a place where the lottery does not make it holy,
phrases.notes: He means other קרבנות, such as the pair of birds a woman brings after giving birth, where there is no lottery.

phrases.english: naming it does make it holy,
then in a place where the lottery does make it holy,
is it not logical that naming makes it holy?
The verse teaches: 'And he shall make it a sin offering' –
the lottery makes it a sin offering,
and naming it does not make it a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that the challenge in step 2 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That a קל וחומר is considered even where the word 'חוקה' is written.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'ועשהו חטאת' (ויקרא 16:9), which needed a פסוק to block the קל וחומר.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's conclusion (naming does not work) is not the point the גמרא cares about. The point is that the ברייתא had to bring a פסוק at all, which shows the קל וחומר would otherwise have worked.

steps.title: So a קל וחומר works even with חוקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes the point: the only reason we skip the קל וחומר on יום הכפורים is the פסוק, so normally a קל וחומר works even where 'חוקה' is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'And he shall make it a sin offering.' Otherwise, we would use the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא and completes its challenge against step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'חוקה' by itself blocked every קל וחומר, the ברייתא would not have needed 'ועשהו חטאת'. Since it did need that פסוק, the word 'חוקה' must not be enough. That contradicts the answer given for the פרה אדומה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is…' – used to make an inference from what a source says
'The Merciful One' – a name for ה׳ as the Author of the תורה
'But if not for this' – the opposite case that follows from the inference

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: on יום הכפורים, which is called a 'חוקה', it took a special פסוק to block a קל וחומר. So 'חוקה' alone does not seem to block a קל וחומר, and the פרה אדומה answer is now in question.

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'And he shall make it a sin offering';

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָאו הָכִי דָּרְשִׁינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר!
phrases.english: but if not for this, we would derive the קל וחומר!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״וְעָשָׂהוּ חַטָּאת״, הָא לָאו הָכִי דָּרְשִׁינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא in steps 2–3 and turns it into a challenge against step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 1's claim that the word 'חוקה' blocks a קל וחומר for the פרה אדומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא needed a special פסוק to block a קל וחומר on יום הכפורים even though the word חוקה is written there. So חוקה alone cannot be what blocks a קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא must now explain what is special about the פרה אדומה, or refine what the word 'חוקה' really teaches.

steps.title: A word in the verse limits neck-breaking to the heifer alone
steps.stepSummary: The real reason the פרה אדומה cannot be done with עריפה is a limiting word in the פסוק about עגלה ערופה. It is not the word 'חוקה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah limited it regarding the עגלה ערופה: 'this one' is done by breaking the neck, and no other animal is done by breaking the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4. It gives a new source for why the פרה אדומה is not done with עריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that 'חוקה' does not block a קל וחומר. So the גמרא needs another reason. The word 'הערופה' means 'this one is broken', so only the עגלה gets עריפה, and the פרה אדומה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') limited it, leaving out other cases
The heifer whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
Breaking the neck from behind with a hatchet

phrases.english: The Merciful One limited it, regarding the heifer whose neck is broken,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:6

phrases.english: 'this one' is done with neck-breaking,
phrases.notes: The word 'הערופה', 'the one whose neck is broken', is read as 'this one and only this one.'

phrases.english: and no other is done with neck-breaking.
phrases.notes: The 'other' one here is the פרה אדומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 by replacing 'חוקה' with a different limiting source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: a limiting word in the פסוק, not 'חוקה'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חוקה' alone is what stops the פרה from being done with עריפה
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'הערופה' limits עריפה to the עגלה, so the פרה needs שחיטה

steps.title: Shouldn't the heifer also be valid with slaughter by a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns things around. If the פרה, which cannot have עריפה, works with שחיטה, then the עגלה, which does work with עריפה, should surely also work with שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the עגלה be valid with שחיטה through a קל וחומר: if the פרה, which is not valid with עריפה, is valid with שחיטה, then the עגלה, which is valid with עריפה, should surely be valid with שחיטה too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges from the other side. Even if the פרה cannot use עריפה, maybe the עגלה can use שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that שחיטה is the 'easier' way, since even the weaker case (the פרה) gets it. So the 'stronger' case (the עגלה, which gets both) should get שחיטה too. Step 5 only blocked עריפה for others; it said nothing about שחיטה for the עגלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Isn't it logical? (the closing words of a קל וחומר)
Was made valid or fit

phrases.aramaic: וּתְהֵא עֶגְלָה כְּשֵׁרָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר:
phrases.english: But let the heifer be valid with slaughter through a kal vachomer:
If the red cow, which is not valid with neck-breaking,
is valid with slaughter,
then the heifer, which is valid with neck-breaking,
isn't it logical that it is valid with slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא עֶגְלָה כְּשֵׁרָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 4's point (a קל וחומר still works) to argue the reverse direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the עגלה ערופה may only be done with עריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the פרה (valid only with שחיטה) to the עגלה (valid with עריפה) would make the עגלה valid with שחיטה too

steps.title: The verse says 'they shall break the neck', so only neck-breaking works
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק, 'וערפו העגלה', teaches that the עגלה needs עריפה and not שחיטה. That blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and they shall break the neck of the heifer': with עריפה, yes; with שחיטה, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6 with another פסוק that blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עריפה is already written once, so mentioning it again in 'וערפו' teaches that only this method works. A פסוק beats a קל וחומר, so the עגלה cannot be done with שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes... no (Aramaic): this way works, that way does not

steps.whatToRemember: Each animal is locked to its own method: the פרה אדומה needs שחיטה because 'הערופה' limits עריפה to the עגלה, and the עגלה ערופה needs עריפה because of 'וערפו'. A קל וחומר can work even with 'חוקה', but a limiting פסוק stops it.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And they shall break the neck of the heifer'
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

phrases.english: with neck-breaking, yes; with slaughter, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6's קל וחומר with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עגלה could also be done with שחיטה through a קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וערפו' teaches that only עריפה works for the עגלה

steps.title: משנה: something valid for priests but invalid for Levites, and the reverse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה states that something can leave כהנים fit but make לוים unfit, and something else can do the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is something that is fit in כהנים but unfit in לוים, and something that is fit in לוים but unfit in כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It states a puzzle without explaining it yet, and the גמרא will explain it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives another pair of opposites, like the פרה and the עגלה. It does not say what the disqualifying thing is. That missing detail is what the ברייתא in the next step fills in.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Fit / unfit for service
Priests, descendants of אהרן, who do the sacrificial service
Levites, who sang and guarded in the מקדש and carried the משכן

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Fit in priests, unfit in Levites;
fit in Levites, unfit in priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the פרה and עגלה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some things disqualify לוים but not כהנים, and other things disqualify כהנים but not לוים

steps.title: Blemishes disqualify priests, but age disqualifies Levites
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה. Physical blemishes disqualify כהנים but not לוים, and age disqualifies לוים but not כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: כהנים are unfit with blemishes but fit no matter how many years they have. לוים are fit with blemishes but become unfit with years. So something fit in כהנים is unfit in לוים, and something fit in לוים is unfit in כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that names the two things the משנה was hinting at: blemishes and age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches each disqualification to one group. A blemish disqualifies a כהן but not a לוי. Age disqualifies a לוי but not a כהן. Both halves of the משנה are now explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Physical blemishes that disqualify a כהן from service
Years, meaning age limits on service
It turns out; it comes out that

steps.whatToRemember: מומין disqualify כהנים, not לוים; age disqualifies לוים, not כהנים. That is the meaning of the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a כהן becomes unfit as he gets older. Age limits apply only to לוים; a כהן without a blemish stays fit his whole adult life.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
Priests: with blemishes they are unfit,
with years they are fit.
Levites: with blemishes they are fit,
with years they are unfit.
phrases.notes: A לוי served only within a set age range, so age can disqualify him. במדבר 4:47

phrases.english: It turns out: fit in priests, unfit in Levites;
fit in Levites, unfit in priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the משנה in Step 8 meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מומין disqualify כהנים but not לוים; age disqualifies לוים but not כהנים

steps.title: What is the source for these rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's rules about כהנים and לוים come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rules just taught: blemishes disqualify כהנים, and age disqualifies לוים. This sets up the next ברייתא, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 gave the rules but no source. Now the גמרא wants to see which פסוקים they come from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where?
These
Matters, things (rules)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the rules from the last ברייתא: blemishes disqualify כהנים, and age disqualifies לוים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rules stated in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches age disqualifies לוים, blemishes do not, and the reverse for כהנים.

steps.title: Age disqualifies the לוים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק says 'זאת אשר ללוים'. It first notes that the פסוק about age fifty teaches that age disqualifies לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'This is what applies to the לוים.' Why does the פסוק need to say this? Since it says 'from age fifty he shall go back from the service', we learn that age disqualifies the לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. First it states the basic fact: once a לוי reaches fifty, he stops serving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks why the extra words 'זאת אשר ללוים' are needed. Before answering, it sets the base fact: age already disqualifies לוים. The next steps will show what the extra words add.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
He shall go back (retire from service)
Years (age)
Make unfit, disqualify
The Levites

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"This is that which pertains to the Levites": why does the verse state this?
phrases.notes: במדבר ח:כד

phrases.english: Since it is stated: "And from the age of fifty years he shall return",
phrases.notes: במדבר ח:כה. 'Return' here means he goes back from the service and stops working.

phrases.english: we learned regarding the Levites that years disqualify them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: זֹאת אֲשֶׁר לַלְוִיִּם מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'from age fifty he shall go back' is the source that age disqualifies לוים.

steps.title: A קל וחומר suggests blemishes should disqualify לוים
steps.stepSummary: Maybe blemishes also disqualify לוים. Age does not disqualify כהנים, yet blemishes do. So for לוים, whom age does disqualify, blemishes should surely disqualify them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think blemishes disqualify them too. It makes sense: כהנים are not disqualified by age, yet they are disqualified by blemishes. לוים are disqualified by age, so shouldn't blemishes disqualify them as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe a לוי with a blemish is also unfit. It backs this up with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that לוים look 'stricter' than כהנים when it comes to age. So it seems they should be at least as strict as כהנים when it comes to blemishes. This is the 'you might think' that the next step will block.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think
It is logical (it can be reasoned out)
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter case
Physical blemishes
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: One might have thought that blemishes disqualify them.
And it is a logical inference:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁאֵין הַשָּׁנִים פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: If priests, whom years do not disqualify,
are disqualified by blemishes,
then Levites, whom years do disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהוּ מוּמִין פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶם?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that blemishes should disqualify them?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל מוּמִין פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶם? וְדִין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact from step 11 that age disqualifies לוים, and uses it to argue that blemishes should too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that blemishes do not disqualify לוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from כהנים: they are not disqualified by age but are disqualified by blemishes. So לוים, who are disqualified by age, should also be disqualified by blemishes.

steps.title: 'This' is for the לוים, and nothing else
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זאת' limits the לוים' disqualification to age alone. Blemishes do not disqualify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'This is what applies to the לוים'. This applies to the לוים, and no other disqualification applies to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the word 'זאת' ('this') to block the קל וחומר. Only age disqualifies לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This' is a limiting word: only this one thing, age, applies to לוים. A פסוק beats a קל וחומר, so blemishes do not make a לוי unfit. This is the first reason the extra words were needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (to teach us)
This (only this)
There is no other
A word in the פסוק that limits a rule

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "This is that which pertains to the Levites":
"This" pertains to the Levites, and no other pertains to the Levites.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the age limit. No other disqualification, like blemishes, applies to לוים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the קל וחומר of step 12 with a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק limits the rule and overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blemishes would disqualify לוים, based on the קל וחומר from כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only age disqualifies לוים. Blemishes do not.

steps.title: A reverse קל וחומר suggests age should disqualify כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Maybe age also disqualifies כהנים. Blemishes do not disqualify לוים, yet age does. So for כהנים, whom blemishes do disqualify, age should surely disqualify them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think כהנים are disqualified by age. It makes sense: לוים are not disqualified by blemishes, yet they are disqualified by age. כהנים are disqualified by blemishes, so shouldn't age disqualify them as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now flips the argument around. It suggests a mistake in the other direction: maybe an old כהן is unfit to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 12. Here כהנים look 'stricter' because of blemishes, so the argument says they should also be strict about age.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it...?
Unfit, disqualified
Priests

phrases.english: One might have thought that priests would be disqualified by years.
And couldn't this be derived logically?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לְוִיִּם שֶׁאֵין מוּמִין פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶם –
phrases.english: If Levites, whom blemishes do not disqualify,
are disqualified by years,
then priests, whom blemishes do disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהוּ שָׁנִים פּוֹסְלִין בָּהֶם?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that years should disqualify them?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים פְּסוּלִין בְּשָׁנִים? וַהֲלֹא דִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 13's result (blemishes do not disqualify לוים) to build a reverse קל וחומר about כהנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that age does not disqualify כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from לוים: they are not disqualified by blemishes but are disqualified by age. So כהנים, who are disqualified by blemishes, should also be disqualified by age.

steps.title: 'For the לוים', not for the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר ללוים' show that the age limit belongs only to the לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'what applies to the לוים', and not what applies to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks the reverse קל וחומר with the words 'for the לוים'. The age limit is a rule for לוים only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same short phrase now teaches a second lesson. 'For the לוים' means not for the כהנים, so an old כהן may still serve.

keyTerms.meaning: Which applies to the לוים
And not what applies to the כהנים
Learning a rule from the words of a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Blemishes disqualify כהנים but not לוים, and age disqualifies לוים but not כהנים. Each half comes from the words 'זאת אשר ללוים', and those words block the two opposite קל וחומר arguments.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "Which pertains to the Levites":
and not which pertains to the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the reverse קל וחומר of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק limits the rule and overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Age would disqualify כהנים, based on the קל וחומר from לוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Age disqualifies only לוים, not כהנים.

steps.title: Does the age limit apply in שילה and the בית המקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether לוים are disqualified by age even in שילה and in the permanent בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the same is true even in שילה and in the בית עולמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question: did the age limit for לוים apply forever, even once the משכן stopped traveling? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we know that age disqualifies לוים. Now the ברייתא asks how far that rule goes in time and place: does it hold even where the משכן stood in one fixed place?

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the משכן stood for many years in ארץ ישראל
The permanent house, meaning the בית המקדש
Even
The same (so)

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף בְּשִׁילֹה וּבְבֵית עוֹלָמִים כֵּן?
phrases.english: One might have thought that even in Shiloh and in the eternal Temple it is so.
phrases.notes: 'It is so' means לוים would still be disqualified at age fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף בְּשִׁילֹה וּבְבֵית עוֹלָמִים כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who is disqualified to when the age disqualification applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the לוים' age limit applies even after the משכן became fixed in one place.

steps.title: The age limit was only for carrying on the shoulders
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links the age limit to 'the work of carrying'. So it applied only while the משכן was carried on the shoulders, in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'to do the work of service and the work of carrying'. I said this only for the time when the work was done on the shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the age limit belonged only to the time when לוים carried the משכן on their shoulders. In שילה and the בית המקדש it did not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'the work of carrying' together with the age rule. That shows the rule was tied to heavy carrying. Once nothing was carried, age no longer disqualified the לוים.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of service
The work of carrying loads
Shoulder
I only said it for...

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדַת עֲבוֹדָה וַעֲבֹדַת מַשָּׂא״,
phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "To perform the work of service and the work of bearing burdens",
phrases.notes: במדבר ד:מז

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה בַּכָּתֵף.
phrases.english: I stated it only at a time when the service is on the shoulder.
phrases.notes: He means carrying the משכן on their shoulders while traveling in the מדבר.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדַת עֲבוֹדָה וַעֲבֹדַת מַשָּׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16: the age rule applied only while the משכן was carried.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The age disqualification applied only when the לוים' service involved carrying on the shoulders, not in שילה or the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Two פסוקים give different starting ages
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says לוים start at 25, and another says they start at 30. Both cannot simply be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says 'from age twenty-five and up', and another says 'from age thirty'. You cannot say thirty, since twenty-five was already said. And you cannot say twenty-five, since thirty was already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a contradiction between two פסוקים about the age at which a לוי begins. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two numbers seem to cancel each other out. If service starts at 30, why does a פסוק say 25? If it starts at 25, why does a פסוק say 30?

keyTerms.meaning: One פסוק says
It is impossible to say
Since it was already said
And up (and older)

phrases.aramaic: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה״,
phrases.english: One verse says: "From twenty-five years old and upward",
phrases.notes: במדבר ח:כד

phrases.english: and one verse says: "From thirty years old",
phrases.notes: במדבר ד:מז

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר שְׁלֹשִׁים, שֶׁכְּבָר נֶאֱמַר חָמֵשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים,
phrases.english: it is impossible to say thirty, as twenty-five was already stated,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר חָמֵשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים, שֶׁכְּבָר נֶאֱמַר שְׁלֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: and it is impossible to say twenty-five, as thirty was already stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ending age of the לוים to a question about their starting age.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about when a לוי begins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two פסוקים give different starting ages, 25 and 30, and each seems to rule out the other.

steps.title: Twenty-five for training, thirty for service
steps.stepSummary: At 25 a לוי begins learning the work, and at 30 he begins actually doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how does it work? Twenty-five is for learning, and thirty is for the actual service.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא settles the contradiction: each age is for a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים do not argue. A לוי trains for five years starting at 25, then begins real service at 30. Each number has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (How do we fit them together?)
For learning (training)
For the actual service

steps.whatToRemember: A לוי trained from 25, served from 30, and stopped at 50. The age-50 limit applied only while the משכן was carried on the shoulders.

phrases.english: How so?
Twenty-five for learning, and thirty for service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק refers to a different stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים contradict each other about the starting age.
steps.terutzMaskana: Twenty-five is the age to begin training, and thirty is the age to begin actual service.

steps.title: A lesson for students: five years without success
steps.stepSummary: From the five years a לוי spends training, we learn that a student who sees no success in five years will not succeed later.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn: a student who has not seen a good sign in his learning after five years will not see one later.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It takes the answer from step 19 (25 to learn, 30 to start working) and turns it into a general life lesson about learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוי trains for exactly five years, from 25 to 30. The Torah set five years as the training time. So the ברייתא learns that five years is the real test period: if a student sees no progress by then, he is unlikely to see it later.

keyTerms.meaning: From here we learn
A good sign, a sign of success
His learning, his studies

phrases.english: From here [we learn] about a student
phrases.notes: "From here" points back to step 19: the five years between age 25 and age 30.

phrases.english: who did not see a good sign in his learning
for five years, will no longer see [one].

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן לְתַלְמִיד שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה סִימָן יָפֶה בְּמִשְׁנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a general lesson about learning on the answer of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who sees no success in his learning within five years will not see it later.

steps.title: רבי יוסי says the test period is three years
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues that the test period is three years, based on how דניאל and his friends were trained in Babylonia.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: three years. It says about דניאל and his friends, "And to raise them for three years," and "to teach them the books and the language of the Chaldeans."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees about the number. He brings פסוקים from דניאל showing that three years of training was enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king of Babylonia gave דניאל and his friends three years to learn the books and language of the Chaldeans. רבי יוסי takes this פסוק in ספר דניאל as the model for how long training takes. That makes three years the test, not five.

keyTerms.meaning: And to raise them (train them)
The language of the Chaldeans (Babylonians)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: three years,
as it says: "And to raise them for three years,"
phrases.notes: דניאל 1:5

phrases.english: "and to teach them the books and the language of the Chaldeans."
phrases.notes: דניאל 1:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 20 on the length of the test period and brings a different source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The test period for a student is three years.

steps.title: Why the first view does not learn from דניאל
steps.stepSummary: The first view says the language of the Chaldeans is easy, so three years was enough for it. That does not set a rule for all learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does the other view handle the פסוק in דניאל? The language of the Chaldeans is different, because it is easy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the five-year view deals with רבי יוסי's proof from דניאל, and answers for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five-year view says the דניאל case does not prove a general rule. A language is light and quick to learn, so three years was enough for that subject only. Harder learning needs a longer test.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning how does the other side explain this?
It is different
Light, easy

phrases.english: And the other [view]?
phrases.notes: This is the five-year view: how does he answer רבי יוסי's proof from דניאל?

phrases.english: The language of the Chaldeans is different, since it is easy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the five-year view against רבי יוסי's proof in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using דניאל as a general model for how long training should take.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The language of the Chaldeans is an easy subject, so its short training time cannot be applied to all learning.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי does not learn from the לוים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the laws of the עבודה are hard, so they needed five years. That does not set a rule for all learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does the other view, רבי יוסי, handle the לוים? The laws of the Temple service are different, because they are hard.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the reverse: how does רבי יוסי deal with the five years of the לוים? It answers for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the לוים case is an exception. The laws of the עבודה are especially difficult, so they needed five years of training. Normal learning gets the shorter three-year test.

keyTerms.meaning: The laws of the Temple service
Strong, hard, difficult

steps.confusionAlert: The two "וְאִידַּךְ" lines point in opposite directions. The first defends the five-year view. This second one defends רבי יוסי's three-year view.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a student has a test period. They argue whether the model is the לוים (5 years) or דניאל (3 years). Each side says the other's example is a special case: the language was easy, the עבודה was hard.

phrases.english: And the other [view]?
The laws of the Temple service are different, since they are hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 22: defends רבי יוסי against the proof from the לוים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the לוים's five-year training as a general model.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The laws of the עבודה are unusually difficult, so their longer training time cannot be applied to all learning.

steps.title: Who is fit for the עבודה: כהן and לוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן serves from physical maturity until old age and only מומין disqualify him. A לוי serves from 30 to 50, and age disqualifies him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a כהן, from when he grows two hairs until he grows old, is fit for the service, and blemishes disqualify him. A לוי from age 30 until age 50 is fit for the service, and age disqualifies him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that compares what makes a כהן fit for the עבודה with what makes a לוי fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כהן, age is not the issue: he serves once he is physically mature, and only a מום (blemish) disqualifies him. For a לוי, it is the opposite: the years themselves decide when he is fit and when he stops.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs, the sign of physical maturity
Until he grows old
Physical blemishes that disqualify a כהן
Disqualify

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: a priest,
from when he grows two hairs until he grows old,
phrases.notes: Two hairs is the standard sign that a boy has physically matured.

phrases.english: is fit for the service, and blemishes disqualify him.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן לֵוִי מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים
phrases.english: A Levite from age thirty until age fifty
is fit for the service, and years disqualify him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֹּהֵן מִשֶּׁיָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת עַד שֶׁיַּזְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side lesson about students and returns to the main topic: the fitness rules for the עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן is disqualified by מומין, not by age. A לוי serves only from 30 to 50.

steps.title: Age only mattered in the מדבר; later only the voice matters
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the age rule to the משכן in the מדבר. In שילה and the בית המקדש, a לוי is disqualified only when his voice fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? In the אהל מועד in the desert. But in שילה and in the permanent בית המקדש, they are disqualified only because of their voice.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא narrows its own rule about the לוי's age. The age limit was only for the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 17: the age limit was tied to carrying the משכן. Once the משכן stood in one place, carrying was over. So what mattered was the לוי's main job of singing, and a failing voice became the only thing that disqualifies him.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (limits the scope of a rule)
The permanent בית המקדש
Voice

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the age limit of 50 does not apply to לוים in the בית המקדש. Only a failing voice disqualifies them there.

phrases.english: When is this said?
In the Tent of Meeting in the desert,
but in Shiloh and in the permanent Temple
they are disqualified only by voice.
phrases.notes: He means: when a לוי's voice is too weak to sing together with the other לוים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the age rule of step 24 to the מדבר only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שילה and the בית המקדש, a לוי is disqualified only by losing his voice, not by age.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי asks which פסוק teaches the rule of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: What is the פסוק for this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי יוסי asks for the פסוק behind the ברייתא's rule, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the rule but gave no source. רבי יוסי wants to show which פסוק teaches it: that in שילה and the בית המקדש a לוי is disqualified only by his voice. His answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? (asks for the Torah source)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source behind the rule in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the age limit applied only in the מדבר and that later only the voice disqualifies a לוי.
